A low, harsh sun draws very long shadows across the scene, all its ground covered in coarse, uneven gravel-like material. Cool cyan shade, bright washed highlights, and a pale hazy sky give this battleground its stark cold-blue cast. Rough, rippled rocky terrain seems to stretch endlessly beyond a broad, roughly square polygonal platform.

Upon it, several dozen pale gray and blue-white masonry buildings gather into a compact, unfinished concrete town. The irregular cluster tightens around a damaged central compound of debris, exposed framework, and a few warm points of light, then thins toward the edges. Broad open yards and winding street-like gaps divide the tighter inner blocks. No marked roads, pavements, vegetation, vehicles, or people interrupt the gravel.

Mostly boxy, flat-roofed buildings rise one to four stories, their varied footprints and heights breaking sightlines rather than forming a regular grid. Weathered plaster upper walls meet darker blue-gray brickwork on lower floors and occasional upper bands. Shallow parapets, barred rectangular windows, rusty boarded or metal door openings, scattered wall-mounted air-conditioning units, and a few narrow projecting balconies mark the façades. Many roofs divide into simple rectangular panels.

Numerous tall, slender rectangular concrete towers punctuate the buildings, open spaces, perimeter, and terrain beyond the platform. Some have tiny square openings; others end in dark vertical slotted caps. The center remains cramped and maze-like, while generous empty ground around the outer buildings makes the transition to the exposed boundary uneven.

A low, harsh sun draws very long shadows across the scene, all its ground covered in coarse, uneven gravel-like material. Cool cyan shade, bright washed highlights, and a pale hazy sky give this battleground its stark cold-blue cast. Rough, rippled rocky terrain seems to stretch endlessly beyond a broad, roughly square polygonal platform.

Upon it, several dozen pale gray and blue-white masonry buildings gather into a compact, unfinished concrete town. The irregular cluster tightens around a damaged central compound of debris, exposed framework, and a few warm points of light, then thins toward the edges. Broad open yards and winding street-like gaps divide the tighter inner blocks. No marked roads, pavements, vegetation, vehicles, or people interrupt the gravel.

Mostly boxy, flat-roofed buildings rise one to four stories, their varied footprints and heights breaking sightlines rather than forming a regular grid. Weathered plaster upper walls meet darker blue-gray brickwork on lower floors and occasional upper bands. Shallow parapets, barred rectangular windows, rusty boarded or metal door openings, scattered wall-mounted air-conditioning units, and a few narrow projecting balconies mark the façades. Many roofs divide into simple rectangular panels.

Numerous tall, slender rectangular concrete towers punctuate the buildings, open spaces, perimeter, and terrain beyond the platform. Some have tiny square openings; others end in dark vertical slotted caps. The center remains cramped and maze-like, while generous empty ground around the outer buildings makes the transition to the exposed boundary uneven.
